nodes.label: Tendril Open Graph Social Preview
nodes.rationale: Dark full-bleed canvas with centered serif wordmark and muted tagline; built as a link-unfurl card, not in-app UI.

nodes.label: The last mile of funding
nodes.rationale: Tagline positions Tendril as completing the final step of funding rather than originating it; muted gray under the wordmark subordinates positioning to brand.

nodes.label: Ephemeral Docker Container Sandbox
nodes.rationale: Trust boundary is not a permissions system but an ephemeral container: no host mounts, no inbound ports (bore dials out), capabilities dropped, cgroup caps, destroyed when the paid lease ends. Same containerization trade-off the DePIN compute sector runs on, made prepaid and individual-scale.

nodes.label: Payment as Identity
nodes.rationale: Payment is the identity: a brand-new address can pay on its very first request with no sign-up or sign-in. Credit is keyed to the sender of the settled transaction, never to anything the client claims about itself.

nodes.label: Verify-Then-Settle Ordering
nodes.rationale: Settlement ordering is verify, do the work, then settle: the facilitator verifies the payment group by simulation, the backend provisions, and only then is payment settled on-chain, so a sandbox that fails to start (503) costs the caller nothing.

nodes.label: Custodial Model
nodes.rationale: Payments pool at one platform address and credit is an off-chain ledger in Neon with one schema per network; every payment is recorded by txid so replaying one cannot credit twice.

nodes.label: Per-Network Ledger Isolation
nodes.rationale: The two ledgers never mix: one database, one Postgres schema per network (testnet.* / mainnet.*), search_path resolves every query to that network's tables, so testnet play money can never be read as a mainnet balance.

nodes.label: CORS-Free Payable Routes
nodes.rationale: Payable routes answer any origin so a browser anywhere can pay one; the Tendril web app has no privileged access and the frontend is just another x402 client. CORS only ever constrained browsers; a headless agent was never subject to it.

nodes.label: MCP Spend Cap (TENDRIL_MAX_ATOMIC)
nodes.rationale: Before paying, the MCP probes the 402 and reads accepts[0].amount; if it exceeds TENDRIL_MAX_ATOMIC it aborts and nothing settles. Withdraw is intentionally not capped this way: it sends existing earnings all-or-nothing.

nodes.label: Linux microVM runtime
nodes.rationale: Firecracker isolates contributor leases; guest filesystems never shared with host.

nodes.label: Cached immutable ext4 guest template
nodes.rationale: Export OCI image once before listing; copy cached template per paid lease and inject credentials offline. Unprepared custom images fail instead of exporting during paid lease.

nodes.label: TENDRIL_RUNTIME selection
nodes.rationale: Auto may fall back to legacy Docker after preflight/cache failure; explicit Firecracker fails startup on missing prerequisites and never retries Docker or Modal after provisioning failure.

nodes.label: Heartbeat runtime and capabilities
nodes.rationale: Capability determines eligibility; idle connected microVMs receive placement priority; missing map fields are false, while absent maps retain legacy SSH/Python support.

nodes.label: Per-guest namespace and TAP networking
nodes.rationale: Namespace-local and lease-owned host NAT permit outbound downloads; TAPs are not LAN bridges, agent opens no inbound TCP, teardown removes forwarding rules.

nodes.label: Jailer ownership and resource bounds
nodes.rationale: Separate agent/VMM cgroups satisfy cgroup v2 no-internal-process rule; quotas, memory overhead, PID/FD caps, guest ulimits and disk size bound resource use.

nodes.label: Platform bore relay manager
nodes.rationale: Separate unprivileged native service controlled by backend over Unix IPC; no public HTTP administration endpoint.

nodes.label: Wildcard DNS and TLS relay
nodes.rationale: Control and notebook traffic use trusted TLS; private raw notebook listener ports remain accessible only to backend on relay host.

nodes.label: Guest SSH, Jupyter and notebook execution
nodes.rationale: Notebook uploads/results use guest Jupyter Contents API; jobs run via papermill over private TAP; Jupyter token remains ephemeral and is never logged or stored in Neon.
nodes.norm_label: guest ssh, jupyter and notebook execution

nodes.label: Lease Release and cleanup protocol
nodes.rationale: First close freezes billing cutoff; peer remains reserved until guest and relay destruction acknowledged. Retried cleanup keeps original cutoff, charge and earnings use lease-ID idempotency keys.

nodes.label: SSH and Jupyter readiness gate
nodes.rationale: Require authenticated guest readiness before activation/settlement; destroy late readiness and avoid charging abandoned or unstarted attempts.

nodes.label: Default P1 CI verification
nodes.rationale: CI verifies contracts without KVM, database, funded wallet or privileged networking.

nodes.label: Opt-in real-kernel KVM gate
nodes.rationale: Dedicated native Linux/KVM host verifies real guest kernel, jailer, networking and relay; skipped command is not a passed kernel gate.

nodes.label: Neon-backed charge replay test
nodes.rationale: Separate database test covers charge replay; KVM harness does not certify on-chain settlement.
